names.note: Read out of the Охридски пролог's heading for 5. мај ст. ст., „Свети Мартин и Ираклије.“ Свети heads both men and is no rank; the heading carries **no rank word at all** and no epithet, no see and no place, so the bare forename is the whole of it. Illyria, which this folder's English name takes, is in the body — „Беху гоњени од јеретика, аријеваца, у Илирији.“ — and not in the heading, and this corpus does not put a place into a name form that the source does not print there. The form meets no other folder in any language, which was measured rather than assumed: `heraclius-companion-of-alexander` holds the fuller Russian «Ираклий Адрианопольский», and `philip-of-heraclea`'s Serbian form carries Ираклијски, which is the see of Heraclea and not this name.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 18.05.2026 (5. мај ст. ст.) — „Свети Мартин и Ираклије.“

attestations.note: **The heading enumerates both men — „Свети Мартин и Ираклије.“ — so the citation above is that heading whole**, per BRIEF-SERBIAN.md §4 and the coordinator's ruling for an enumerated company, and the two names are two folders. **He is new and not an upgrade, and that was measured three ways**: the day list for the menologion 5/5 names eleven folders and neither of these two is among them; `ls saints | grep -iE 'martin|heracl|herakl'` returns twenty-one folders, every one of which is a different man on a different day — seven Martins off Greek and Romanian lines for 10 and 12 November, 7 December and 22 September, and the Heracliuses of Athens, Adrianople, Carthage, Todi, Bessarabia and 14 July — and `grep -ril illyri saints/` returns **no folder at all**, so nothing in this corpus has yet held an Illyrian. The §7 namesweep ranked the seven Martins `!!` on the forename and, as on every enumerated company so far, **read only the first name of the heading**, so Ираклије was swept by hand. The identification is a pair of Slavs persecuted by Arians in Illyria, exiled, and dead in exile in the fourth century. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion.

death.note: Охридски пролог за 5. мај ст. ст.: „Послани у изгнанство ови витези Православља скончаше земни живот у IV веку, и преселише се ка Господу.“ — the book prints the century and no year, and nothing narrower was taken from the Arian persecution it names. `node .tmp/dd.mjs "4th century"` reads it as «IV в.» and «4ος αι.»
